item.title: ISO 9001 Documented Information: the complete guide to Clause 7.5
item.dc:creator: juliana-geremias
item.content:encoded:
Conteudo de demonstracao. Este texto existe para o tema ter o que exibir no ambiente de teste. Substitua pelo artigo real antes de publicar.

What counts as documented information, how long to retain it, and the review workflow auditors actually want to see.

What the standard actually asks for

Requirements are written to be auditable, not to be prescriptive. That gap is where most teams get stuck: the clause says what has to be demonstrable, and leaves the method to the organisation.

  • Define the outcome before choosing the tool.
  • Keep the record proportional to the risk.
  • Review on a cadence someone actually owns.

Where it breaks in practice

The failure is rarely the process on paper. It is the handover between the person who designed it and the people who run it every day.

A process nobody owns is a process nobody runs.
item.excerpt:encoded: What counts as documented information, how long to retain it, and the review workflow auditors actually want to see.
